newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- JUNE 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- JUNE 24.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:

--A new bill submitted to Parliament yesterday by Deputy Finance Minister George Drys is an attempt to rationalise losses from tax debts still outstanding to the state and thought to total 1.6 trillion drachmas.

--State-run companies and organisations involved in telecommunications, electricity, transport and water supply will have signed contracts totalling one trillion drachmas by the end of the year, according to reports, with OTE - Greece's telecoms organisations - and DEH - the state electrical power company - making up the lion's share.
--Drys's bill on a new tax penalty system foresees ten changes to fines and dozens of favourable settlements for firms involved in past violations in an effort to make the tax system more realistic.

--The mini-slump on the Athens Stock Exchange - the general price index yesterday fell another 2.16 percent to end at 1,450 points - provoked an urgent meeting called by the National Bank and attended by a number of representatives from brokerage firms. Reports say there will be coordinated action at today's session to shore up defence against profiteering.
--Development Minister Vasso Papandreou chaired a meeting on speeding up procedures for the signing of contracts in the sectors of energy, telecoms and water resources yesterday.
--Small and medium size enterprises in mainland Greece will get a 37.1 billion drachma injection of capital from the regional investment programme.

--The cancellation of up to 30 domestic flights by Olympic Aviation due to a technician's strike have struck a blow to tourism and the economy. Almost all the flights were destined for the Aegean islands. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
